reconcile.note: Henry reads the stop at Annas as a brief consultative halt before Jesus was sent on to Caiaphas, where the Synoptic trial took place.

discrepancy.note: Strauss treats the synoptic 'high priest' and John's Annas as first stops that cannot both be true, calling the accounts flatly at odds.

quotes.text: the synoptists state Jesus to have been led to the high priest… while John represents him as being led in the first instance to Annas… in this irreconcilable divergency…
quotes.attr: D. F. Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined (1846), §128.

sides.snippet: Those who had taken Jesus led him away to Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and the elders were gathered together.
sides.verseText: Those who had taken Jesus led him away to Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and the elders were gathered together.

sides.snippet: and led him to Annas first, for he was father-in-law to Caiaphas, who was high priest that year.
sides.verseText: and led him to Annas first, for he was father-in-law to Caiaphas, who was high priest that year.
